controller_name: Prior ProScan III (H117 stage, STAGE-based detect)

communication.notes: v7.5.x: real-hardware variant for a Prior ProScan III unit (ME3B V3) identifying as 'H117P1N4/F' via STAGE (the '/F' = Hardware Rev F, confirmed to support 115200 -- Rev F/USB-FTDI boards only, per Prior's 'ProScan III Communication Speed' technical note). This unit was found on 2026-07-23 sitting at the 9600 factory/fail-safe default (no DIP switch exists for baud on ProScan -- confirmed absent from the full official manual -- it's a firmware/EEPROM setting, changed via the documented BAUD,<code> command: 96/19/38/115 for 9600/19200/38400/115200), then bumped live to 115200 (the max) via BAUD,115 and verified. Prior's manual documents that a changed baud reverts to the 9600 default if the port sits idle across TWO power cycles -- baud_rates lists all 3 realistic states (115200 preferred, then 38400, then 9600) so detection self-heals through that reversion without operator intervention; see ControllerProtocol.baud_rate_candidates.

detection.notes: v7.5.x: this unit's 'V' (firmware_version) query returns a bare 'R' ack instead of a version string (confirmed live, isolated, generous-timeout probes at BOTH 9600 and 38400 -- not a baud/timing artifact, a genuine firmware behavior), so proscan_iii.json's V-based detection can never match it at any baud. 'STAGE' reliably returns a rich multi-line descriptor ('STAGE = H117P1N4/F\rTYPE = 25\r...') that IS a genuine, distinctive Prior signature -- used here as both the wake (drains/settles the link before the real query) and the actual detection query. wake_delay_ms raised to 300 (from proscan_iii.json's 100) because the full multi-line reply must have COMPLETELY arrived before the wake-step read+reset, or trailing bytes contaminate the following detection query -- confirmed empirically: a 300ms post-DTR settle alone produced a truncated/spurious 'R' on the first STAGE call, a ~600ms total settle produced the clean full reply every time. response_pattern intentionally omitted (multi-line reply; tokens are enough and safer than a regex across only the first captured line).
